description: The QuickMount pressure-locking retainer: the C-loop that hangs under a mount plate and grips the board. The section is measured off the OEM plate in enclosure_125b/dwg/125B_quickmount.stl; every envelope callout is then verified against the six OEM drawings in ref/quickmount_drawings, and the verification block records each one. The reference type is A/E: Type A is the drawing that matches the Type E plate the calipers were taken on.

measurement.how: planar sections of the OEM mesh: z = 11 cuts one loop's whole section, y = 5 and y = 7.2 bracket the ledge, y = 1.5 and y = 2.95 cut the plate, x = 0 and y = 0 give the plate outline
measurement.axis_convention: in the mesh, x is the plate's 120 mm width, z its 65 mm depth, y runs 0..19.65 away from the pedal with the plate at y = 0..3

mechanism.summary: A closed C-loop hangs under the plate and straddles one board rib, a leg down each slot. The loop is a snap: pressed on, the ledges ride the rib's flanks and spread the legs, and once past the sheet they spring back so the ledge's upward face sits under the sheet. Pedal load then runs plate, post, arch and ledge into the sheet, so pressure tightens the grip instead of working it loose.
mechanism.retention: positive: the ledge's upward face sits under the sheet, so lift is a hard stop, not friction
mechanism.preload: the 3-4 mm board-side foam insert, compressed between plate and board, presses the blade tips up and levers the ledges outward under the sheet
mechanism.release: lever a blade inward until its ledge clears the rib flank, then lift; that is the QuickRelease Tool's job
mechanism.seating: the ledge face sets the depth; there is nothing else to bottom out on
mechanism.extrusion_axis: along the plate's slot, which is the retainer's 22 mm

provenance.source: section shape read off detail C of Type A/D/E/H and detail B of Type M, plus the measured step in the mesh at y = 5 versus y = 7.2

frame.origin: mouth centreline, on the plate underside (the board-facing face)
frame.x: across the mouth; the direction the ledge lock reaches out
frame.y: along the plate's slot; the loop is extruded along this axis
frame.z: toward the pedal; the loop occupies z < 0, and the legs stop at the plate's top face at z = 3
frame.note: The mesh's axes are rotated against these; the measurement block records the mapping.

derived.loop_drop_mm: drop_below_plate_top - plate_thickness = 15.89 below the plate underside
derived.height_total_mm: 18.89: the legs stop at the plate's top face, so the retainer is exactly the drawn drop and the 2.30 ear belongs to the plate
derived.slot_clearance_mm: the 22 retainer sits in the plate's 24 slot, 1.00 a side. The slot is the opening in the plate itself, not the board's slot grid

width.source: 22 callout on Type A and Type E, and 22 with calipers on the owned Type E

drop.source: 18.89 printed on the Type A front view and the Type A/D/H/M end views; the calipers agree to the hundredth

outer_width.source: 19.0 with calipers on a Type E at its widest, where the step is. Neither Type A nor Type E prints this dimension, and Type M's 19.7 does not transfer because it is a different plate

ear_and_slot.source: 24 on the clip ear of Type A and Type E; 24 for the plate's own slot with calipers on a Type E

ear_above_plate.source: 21.19 overall on Type H less the 18.89 drop

derived.arch_wall_mm: half_outer - half_mouth = 3.00, and the arch is a true semicircle centred at z = -(15.89 - 9.50) = -6.39
derived.blade_outer_width_mm: 2 x (half_mouth + blade_wall) = 16.80, the width the blade presents to the plate
derived.arm_below_ledge_mm: 6.39 - 4.00 = 2.39 of straight arm between the ledge and the arch centre
derived.blade_tip: flush with the plate's top face, 0.60 chamfered on the outboard edge, passing through the plate's own slot
derived.wall_budget_mm: outer - mouth = 6.00, and the calipers divide it exactly into post 3.00 + blade 1.90 + step 1.10

measured.the_mouth: 13.0 with inside jaws on a Type E, and Type A's own section scales to 12.99 against its 111.7 callout, so the drawing and the calipers agree. Neither sheet prints it, so the measurement sets the section
measured.the_walls: 3.0 at mid height on the stout leg, 1.9 at the thinnest above the step, and 1.0-1.2 across the step. These sum to the 6.00 that 19.0 less 13.0 leaves, so all four readings are one consistent set
measured.the_blade: 1.9 at its thinnest, above the step
measured.the_flare: 3.5 at the thickest just below the step, about 0.5 more than the 3.00 arm. Read as a fillet at the ledge's root and not modelled
measured.the_ledge_drop: 4.0 from the plate's underside to the step's flat, with calipers
measured.the_arch: 9.50 outer and 6.50 inner about z = -6.39, bottom at -15.89

provenance.source: calipers on the owned Type E for the envelope and every wall, with the mouth independently confirmed by Type A's section C scaled against its own 111.7 callout

derived.spread_per_leg_mm: the step stands 1.10 proud of the blade, so the blade has to move 1.10 inboard to let its ledge ride past a sheet edge and snap back under it
derived.bite_mm: the same 1.10 is the ledge's reach under the sheet
derived.post_side: the post's outer face is already on the 19.00 envelope, so the post side is the rigid side of the loop
derived.not_derived_from_the_board: the spread comes from the retainer's own step, not from a slot width, because no reference states the board's slot

spread.source: 1.0-1.2 measured across the step on a Type E, and 1.10 by arithmetic from the measured walls

wall_min_mm.source: smallest wall that prints reliably at a 0.4 mm nozzle

actuator.location: board side, between the plate's underside and the board
actuator.role: the pad is the vibration dampener and the vertical pressure provider: compressed, it pushes the plate up, which presses the blade tips up and levers the ledges outward under the sheet

derived.pad_needs_a_slot: the loop must pass through the pad to reach the board, so the pad has a cut-out over each retainer; the 4.00 ledge drop is set by the board's sheet, not by the pad
derived.clearance_at_the_retainer_mm: with the sheet's underside at 4.00 below the plate underside and a 3.0 sheet, the sheet's top face stands 1.00 below the plate, which is what the pad compresses to where a retainer passes through

provenance.source: Warwick supplies a 3-4 mm foam insert as a vibration dampener and vertical pressure provider

board_requirement.rib_fit: tight; the mouth is deliberately not a sliding fit, so the loop comes onto the rib with interference and has to be pressed home
board_requirement.note: the retainer fixes one number on the board: the sheet's underside has to fall 4.00 below the plate's underside for the ledge to catch it. Slot pitch, rib and slot width are board properties that no retainer drawing states, so they stay null rather than guessed

provenance.source: no drawing or mesh dimension; confirm on the board before printing
typical datasheet values for the printed filament; the OEM part is a carbon reinforced composite

bend.model: snap-fit cantilever: strain = 1.5 * wall * spread / flexure_length^2, with the flexure taken as the developed centreline of the compliant loop and the wall taken as the thickest material the ledge has to bend, since the ledge sits at the arch end of the blade and cannot move without bending the arch.

provenance.source: standard snap-fit sizing; the generator reports the margin

array.rule: retainers on one plate sit a whole number of board pitches apart, each over its own rib

provenance.source: 33.43 and 64.5 from the Type M end view, 111.7 from the Type A, E, G and H sections

verification.method: read every callout that touches the retainer off the six drawing plates, compare with the section measured off the OEM mesh, then check both against calipers on an owned Type E. Calipers outrank both, but only where they agree with a source; a lone low caliper reading on a curved surface is treated as an under-read, not as a new nominal.
verification.type_equivalence: Type A and Type E are one retainer moulding - the calipers on a Type E read 18.89, exactly what the Type A front view prints, and Type A's section C scales to the same 13.0 mouth the calipers read. So a Type A callout is a statement about the owned Type E plate. The other four plates are different mouldings and their callouts do not transfer: Type M prints 19.7 across the loop where the Type E measures 19.0, which is exactly the sort of difference that makes a callout type-specific.
verification.fit_policy: the reference documents are Type A and Type E, which are one retainer moulding. A value printed on either sheet governs; the calipers fill in what neither sheet states - the outer width, the mouth, the walls, the ledge drop and the plate's slot. Callouts unique to Type D, G, H or M are recorded but not carried into the model, because those plates are different mouldings.

mesh_cross_check.verdict: the mesh confirms the mechanism and three dimensions outright - 22, the 4.00 ledge drop and the semicircular arch - but its section is not the one the Type E shows. Its clip is the third-party reference part: the arch span 16.80, arch base to apex 9.65, arch wall 2.50 and blade 1.20 all reproduce the reference clip measured into catalog/clips/reference_2space_clip.yaml (16.8, 9.64, 2.5, 1.2) exactly, and that part is a different moulding from the OEM Type A/E. So the mesh is used here to corroborate the mechanism, not to set the section
mesh_cross_check.also_noted: the mesh's two clip centres are 95.50 apart, which is 2.86 of the drawn 33.43 pitch rather than a whole number, so that plate's clips do not sit on the board's rib grid as drawn. Worth remembering when the plate generator is written - a pair has to be a whole number of pitches apart

section_shape: All six detail views show the same loop: one stout leg reading straight into the plate, one thin leg, a semicircular arch joining them, and a ledge stepping outward on the thin leg's outer face with its flat side toward the plate.
Type H's left loop measures out at roughly a 15.0 mouth, 1.2 blade, 2.0-2.5 post and a 3.6 ledge drop on an 8 px/mm raster, which agrees with the mesh inside the reading error.
Type M's 63.2 and 68.76 views show the same loop section, so the Type G plate's deep tray sits outside the retainer rather than changing it.

provenance.source: all six plates in ref/quickmount_drawings, plus the ink-metrology reads of the Type H end view

fabrication.print_orientation: plate face down, loop rising; the loop's plane stands vertical so every filament follows the post, the arch and the blade
fabrication.note: the exported STL is in assembly orientation, so rotate 180 deg about X to print

open_questions: No drawing or mesh states the board's slot width, pitch or rib. The mouth is 13.00 and the outer width 18.85 as now settled, so the loop accepts a rib up to 13.00; which board feature it straddles still has to be settled on the board.
The ledge sits 4.00 below the plate's underside. That single number is the contract between retainer and board: the sheet's underside has to be there.

The blade tip is flush with the plate's top face and sits in the plate's own slot, so a plate generator must provide that slot and the 24 mm ear around it. Type A's section B-B suggests the slot is 4 wide with an 82.5 deg, 1 deep chamfer, which is wider than the 1.6 blade and is the next thing to confirm on the plate.

Type A and Type E are one retainer moulding, so the Type A drawing governs the owned Type E plate: 22, 24, 18.89, 3.0, 111.7, 112.4, 102 x 61, 51 hole pitch, 4 mm holes and the 82.5 deg chamfered slot all apply as printed. The two retainer dimensions neither sheet prints are the outer width and the mouth, and the calipers settle both at 19.0 and 13.0.
notes: The retainer is drawn at the plate's edge on a 24 mm ear, with the loop inboard of it; the ear and the blade slot belong to the plate.
18.89 runs from the plate's top face to the loop's lowest point, so the loop below the plate's underside is 15.89, not 18.89.
Type E's 23 and Type G's 28.7 both measure from a raised rim, which is why they exceed the flat-plate 18.89 and why they are not treated as disagreements.
A plate wants a pair of these mirrored about its centre, one at each end, which is how all six drawings lay their retainers out.

Type A's section C is the single most useful view in the set: it draws the loop across the mouth at drawing scale and prints 111.7 on the same view, so an undimensioned section can be read off it at 7.851 px/mm. That is how the 13.0 mouth was confirmed before the calipers arrived.
The Type A sheet also gives the plate's own numbers: 102 x 61 plan, 51 hole pitch, 4 mm holes, 112.4 overall length, and the 82.5 deg chamfered slot in section B-B.

The reference types are A and E, and only those two. Their printed numbers are used wherever they give one; the calipers supply the rest. Type M's 19.7 across the loop is deliberately not used, which is why the envelope is 19.0 and the walls are 3.00 / 1.90 / 1.10 rather than 3.35 / 1.90 / 1.45.
The plate's own slot is 24 wide against a 22 retainer, so 1.00 a side. The word slot here means the opening in the plate that the retainer sits in, not a feature of the board.
